answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, non-transferable deposit before it can post jobs or claim rewards; peers slash that stake when signed work proofs show fraud, while honest completion returns it. This makes a Sybil swarm costly: splitting into many identities means funding a deposit for each, and evasion risks losing them. A haven reputation may help a newcomer, but pigment or onyx labels alone cannot bypass the stake.
